implementation_notes: Node has no scheduling or health framework, but the local idiom replaces the classic monitor entirely: each subscription arms a setTimeout for the silence budget, clears and re-arms it on every message, and the callback firing is the absence alarm - the pending timer is the last-seen state. Measure with performance.now() or process.hrtime.bigint() (monotonic), never Date.now(), and unref() background monitors so a stalled flow cannot keep the process alive on its own. Escalation stays an ordinary emitter chain: the expiry handler emits an event that a notifier (chat, pager, metrics) consumes; a central registry object is only needed once the watched set becomes dynamic or large.
pitfalls: setTimeout delays above 2**31-1 ms (about 24.8 days) overflow the 32-bit delay and fire almost immediately, so a naive long silence budget alerts at once; cap the delay or chain timers.
An un-cleared timer keeps the event loop alive: watchers in tests and in short-lived jobs hang the process unless the timer is cleared on shutdown and unref'd.
setInterval re-arms itself even while the previous async check is still running and drifts under load; for detection prefer a single resettable setTimeout whose deadline comes from the last arrival.
Date.now() is wall-clock, so a DST fall-back or an NTP step looks like extra silence (or erases real silence); always stamp with performance.now().
clearTimeout after the callback already ran is a no-op and leaves no alert state behind: without an explicit silent/alarmed state machine, recovery and repeat-while-silent cannot be expressed.
